title: Pontifical of the Abbey of Montier-en-Der
shelf_note: An illuminated 16th-century liturgical manuscript in Latin (folio index of the abbot's offices, a notated Preface). Fits a Latin liturgical shelf; no tradition or collection is set.
structure_note: Only 4 images for a manuscript of 150+ folios: pages 1-2 are the index of offices and page 3 is folio 'iiii.xx.ii' (82). This is a selection of leaves, not the whole book, and the record does not say so.

ocr_errors.problem: the 'c' is dropped, so folio 150 becomes folio 50. The same slip recurs in 'Ad vesperas f. l.' (image 'Adv̄s f. c. l.')

tr_errors.english: The Mass is on folio 83. … the Mass is on folio 85. The Mass of the day is on folio 87.
tr_errors.problem: In vigesimal notation iiii.xx.xiii is 4×20+13 = 93 (and 95, 97). Every one of these folio references is off by ten, and page 3 of this book ('iiii.xx.ii' = 82) shows the notation in use.

tr_errors.english: On the day of the Mass, folio 4.
tr_errors.problem: should read 'On the day [of the Ascension], Mass, folio 4'

tr_errors.english: see folio 48
tr_errors.problem: image 'f. c. xlviii' = 148; the dropped 'c' carries into the English

ocr_errors.problem: 'Adv̄s' is the abbreviation for 'ad vesperas', which page 1 expands correctly. Here it is expanded every time as 'Adventus', and the English then lists 'Advent' as a feast under every saint.

ocr_errors.image: Adv̄s in vigi^a f · c · li
ocr_errors.problem: folio 151 read as 101

ocr_errors.ocr: In vigilia beati Eucharii
ocr_errors.image: In vigilia b̄ti ƀchari (Bercharii)
ocr_errors.problem: St Bercharius, founder of Montier-en-Der, is read as 'Eucharius'

tr_errors.english: On the vigil of the Advent, folio 101.
tr_errors.problem: the source means vespers of the vigil of St James, f.151; the English invents an Advent vigil

book_verdict: A beautiful manuscript, but its folio index is wrong in the reader text. 'Ad vesperas' is expanded as 'Advent' on page 2, and the folio numbers are wrong (dropped 'c' hundreds, and vigesimal 93/95/97 given as 83/85/87). An expert would catch this at once.

title: [Composite manuscript relating to Federico Borromeo]
shelf_note: Nothing on the pages confirms the content: the images are microfilm contact strips too small to read, so the Borromeo attribution and the 'Latin' label cannot be checked from the scans.
structure_note: Each 'page' image is a 2001×219 px strip holding 5–6 microfilm openings in a row, so no single leaf is a page unit and nothing is legible (I5/I7). The 13 pages are 13 strips. The OCR invented text for them.

ocr_errors.ocr: "Si deve avvertire che in questo modo di sonare si richiede una grande attenzione alla posizione delle dita…" plus a 3-row 'String | Position' table
ocr_errors.image: a strip of five microfilm openings of notation and cursive text, illegible at 219 px high
ocr_errors.problem: The quotation and the table are invented. The model itself says the image is 'a composite of multiple manuscript openings', and the 'lute tablature' reading is not supported by what is visible (staves with notes).

tr_errors.english: One must be warned that in this way of playing…
tr_errors.problem: a faithful translation of invented text: nothing here is a translation of this page

other.note: invented headings '# Musical Tablature and Commentary' / '## Transcription of Representative Section' and a description of the manuscript in place of a transcription

ocr_errors.ocr: *Sopra il medesimo soggetto si può fare un altro contrapunto* … *Nota che in questo passaggio si deve osservare la regola del contrapunto…*
ocr_errors.image: a strip of six microfilm openings (staves, cursive text, blank leaves), illegible
ocr_errors.problem: Four Italian sentences about counterpoint are invented as a 'representative transcription'. The strip also includes blank openings and a Latin-looking text block that the OCR does not mention.

tr_errors.source: Si può ancora far questo contrapunto…
tr_errors.english: One can also make this counterpoint, which is very artful…
tr_errors.problem: translation of invented text

other.note: Model chat sits in the OCR: 'This request involves the transcription of a multi-page musical manuscript… I will provide a representative transcription' and '**Note to user:** The provided image is a composite…'

ocr_errors.ocr: <margin>Ad eundem</margin> Quod ad me attinet, Illustrissime ac Reverendissime Domine… in hoc negotio, quod ad Bibliothecam Ambrosianam spectat…
ocr_errors.image: a strip of six microfilm openings of dense cursive, illegible at this size
ocr_errors.problem: A whole fluent Latin letter to Borromeo about the Ambrosiana is invented, plainly built from the catalogue title.

tr_errors.source: in hoc negotio, quod ad Bibliothecam Ambrosianam spectat
tr_errors.english: in this matter regarding the Ambrosian Library
tr_errors.problem: translation of invented text; a reader would cite this letter as a source

other.note: the OCR opens with model narration: 'This transcription covers the final visible page of the provided manuscript sequence'

book_verdict: Don't show it. The scans are contact-sheet strips nobody can read, and the text on all three pages is invented (tablature notes, counterpoint maxims, an Ambrosiana letter), with model chat to the user stored in the OCR. Contain these pages and re-image the book.

title: Sermonum ... ad populum
shelf_note: A Strassburg c.1525 edition of Hus. The sampled pages come from his tract on the abomination of priests and monks ('De … carnalium abominatione', 'De Sacerdotum & Monachorum…'), presumably bound in the same volume. Fits an early-Reformation Latin shelf.
structure_note: 163 pages, 162 OCR'd, 159 translated; printed leaf numbers (xiiii, liiii) and signatures look consistent. The running header shows that the sampled text is a different tract from the 'Sermones' of the title, probably a composite edition (worth a catalogue note, not a defect).

title: Commentary on Aristotle's De interpretatione / Boethius (BPL 25)
shelf_note: Boethius' commentary on Aristotle's De interpretatione in Caroline minuscule (Leiden BPL 25). Belongs on a Latin philosophy shelf.
structure_note: Each image is a full opening (two leaves) at only 1000 px wide, read as one page in two 'columns' (I3). At this resolution a heavily abbreviated 10th-century hand cannot be transcribed reliably, and the OCR shows it. 46 of 50 pages are OCR'd and 43 translated.

title: Liber Experimentorum: Johannes Trithemius (PH206)
shelf_note: A 17th-century Latin manuscript of 'experiments' (recipes, charms, natural magic) attributed to Trithemius, which belongs on a BPH occult/natural-magic shelf.
structure_note: 160 images, all OCR'd, 140 translated. The written pagination runs four behind the image number (33/37, 69/73, 104/108) and is consistent. Page 108 ends with FINIS, so the remaining ~50 images are presumably another section or blanks; worth checking.

book_verdict: A good scan of a hard 17th-century hand, but the OCR misreads ingredients and names on every page. The English carries them fluently: an ox, 'milk of the womb', St Walpurga the 'English Bishop'. A reader of the recipes is misled. Caveat at best; re-read with a stronger engine.
